s: Corinna has stomach smooth
q: How smooth her stomach beneath her faultless bosom!

s: Corinna has sides full and beauteous
q: How full and how beauteous her sides!

s: Corinna has thighs plump with youthfulness
q: How plump with youthfulness the thigh!

s: Corinna is beautiful beauteous
q: Nothing did I behold not worthy of praise; and I pressed her person even to my own.

s: Naso is lover of Corinna
q: Nothing did I behold not worthy of praise; and I pressed her person even to my own.

s: Naso is a lover
q: ELEGY VI. _He entreats the porter to open to him the door of his mistress's house._

s: porter guards mistress's house (at its threshold)
q: It becomes you not to watch the threshold of the beauteous fair

s: porter is a slave (subject to long fetters)
q: may you one day be liberated from your long fetters and may the water of the slave [068] be not for ever drunk of by you.

s: door (mistress's door) is stubborn hard (with a turning hinge)
q: throw open the stubborn door with its turning hinge.

s: door (mistress's door) has the bar (from the door-post)
q: from the door-post [067] strike away the bar.

s: door-post supports door (mistress's door) (as part of the doorway)
q: the door, supported by its hard oaken _posts_, is still unmoved.

s: Cupid becomes bold
q: Cupid, with his graceful mother, laughed, so that I could hear him, and he softly said, "Thou too wilt become bold."

s: Venus is the mother of Cupid (graceful)
q: Cupid, with his graceful mother, laughed, so that I could hear him

s: keepers has mistress's house
q: 'Tis he who shows me how to go softly amid the watches of the keepers

s: night is without shame (as an influence on the lover)
q: Night, and lore, and wine, [075] are persuasive of no moderation; the first is without shame

s: Naso has body thin (through prolonged Love)
q: Protracted Love has made my body thin for such an emergency

s: chaplet is worn by Naso (on his anointed hair)
q: the chaplet falling from off my anointed hair

s: wind shakes door (mistress's door) (boisterously)
q: the door was shaken by the boisterous wind.

s: enemy shuts out door (mistress's door)
q: What would you do to an enemy, who thus shut out the lover?

s: Naso is guided by Cupid (in moving safely past the keepers)
q: 'tis he directs my feet that meet no harm.

s: Naso courts Corinna
q: I only fear you, _thus_ too tardy; you alone do I court

s: Naso possesses sword (while attempting to scale the house)
q: Otherwise I, myself, [073] now better prepared _than you_, with my sword

s: Naso possesses torch (holding fire in it)
q: and with the fire which I am holding in my torch

s: Naso accompanies wine (about his temples)
q: Love then, and a little wine about my temples, [069] are with me

s: Naso wears chaplet (falling from his anointed hair)
q: and the chaplet falling from off my anointed hair

s: porter is fastened with the cruel fetter
q: Porter, fastened (_and_ how unworthily!) with the cruel fetter

s: Naso is a lover (of the mistress)
q: He has beaten his mistress, and endeavours to regain her favour.

s: Dipsas advises mistress (in the arts of a courtesan)
q: He curses a certain procuress, whom he overhears instructing his mistress in the arts of a courtesan.

s: mistress is beautiful beauty (inferior to no one's)
q: And whom do you not please? Your beauty is inferior to no one's.

s: mistress is sought by the wealthy young man (as a lover)
q: a rich lover is sighing for you, and he makes it his care [107] what are your requirements

s: Venus favors mistress (through her planetary influence)
q: The adverse star of Mars in opposition [106] was unfortunate for you; Mars has gone; now Venus is befriending you with her planet

s: the lovers makes presents (it is a noble thing to give)
q: The God himself of poets, graceful in his mantle [116] adorned with gold, strikes the harmonious strings of the gilded lyre. He that shall make you presents, let him be to you greater than great Homer; believe me, it is a noble thing to give

s: the lovers are manipulated by the courtesan's trade (through feigned affection, refusal, jealousy, and deception)
q: Pretended affection, too, is not a bad thing; let him fancy he is loved; but have you a care that this affection is not all for nothing.

s: the presents and payments extracted from lovers are sought by the sister of the damsel (as part of a collective exaction)
q: Let your sister, and your mother, and your nurse as well, fleece your admirer. A booty is soon made, that is sought by many hands.

s: the presents and payments extracted from lovers are sought by the mother of the damsel (as part of a collective exaction)
q: Let your sister, and your mother, and your nurse as well, fleece your admirer. A booty is soon made, that is sought by many hands.

s: Naso causes the beating of the mistress (through frenzied violence)
q: For frenzy has raised my rash arms against my mistress; hurt by my frantic hand, the fair is weeping.

s: the presents and payments extracted from lovers are sought by the nurse of the damsel (as part of a collective exaction)
q: Let your sister, and your mother, and your nurse as well, fleece your admirer. A booty is soon made, that is sought by many hands.

s: the courtesan's trade uses the male servant (as a trained intermediary)
q: Let a male servant and a crafty handmaid [129] be trained up to their parts; who may instruct him what may be conveniently purchased for you

s: the courtesan's trade uses the crafty handmaid (as a trained intermediary)
q: Let a male servant and a crafty handmaid [129] be trained up to their parts; who may instruct him what may be conveniently purchased for you

s: the courtesan's trade invokes Isis (as a pretext for refusing a lover)
q: Often refuse your favours; sometimes pretend a head-ache; and sometimes there will be Isis [121] to afford a pretext

s: the lovers are exploited by the courtesan's trade (through rivalry and jealousy)
q: Take care that no one loves you in security, without a rival; love is not very lasting if you

s: mistress is a free-born woman
q: But now, in the hardness of my heart, I could dare, seizing her hair on her forehead, to mark her free-born cheeks [090] with my nails

s: mistress is beautiful beauty
q: And whom do you not please? Your beauty is inferior to no one's.

s: Dipsas is a old hag (and procuress)
q: There is a certain old hag, Dipsas by name.

s: Dipsas is a procuress
q: There is a certain--(whoever wishes to make acquaintance with a procuress, let him listen.)--There is a certain old hag, Dipsas by name.

s: Dipsas is often drunk drunkenness (never sober when observing the dawn)
q: From fact does she derive [094] her name; never in a sober state does she behold the mother of the swarthy Memnon with her horses of roseate hue

s: Dipsas knows magic (well)
q: She knows well the magic arts, and the charms of Ææa, [095] and by her skill she turns back to its source [096] the flowing stream

s: Dipsas knows Ææa (its charms)
q: She knows well the magic arts, and the charms of Ææa, [095] and by her skill she turns back to its source [096] the flowing stream

s: Atticus is addressed by Naso (as the recipient of the elegy)
q: believe me, Atticus, [138] every lover is a soldier.

s: anxious lover takes advantage of sleep of husband (to attack the sleeping rival)
q: Full oft do lovers take advantage of the sleep of husbands, and brandish their arms against the slumbering foe.

s: anxious lover evades sentinels (as part of the lover's persistent hardship)
q: To escape the troops of the sentinels, and the bands of the patrol, is the part _both_ of the soldier, and of the lover always in misery.

s: anxious lover evades patrol (as part of the lover's persistent hardship)
q: To escape the troops of the sentinels, and the bands of the patrol, is the part _both_ of the soldier, and of the lover always in misery.

s: Love belongs to discerning mind (rather than mere slothfulness)
q: Whoever, then, has pronounced Love _mere_ slothfulness, let him cease _to love_: [144] to the discerning mind does Love belong.

s: Achilles is inflamed by Briseis (the captive Briseis)
q: The mighty Achilles is inflamed by the captive Briseis.

s: Trojans are urged to destroy Argive resources (while they have the opportunity)
q: Trojans, while you may, destroy the Argive resources.

s: Hector is husband of Andromache
q: Hector used to go to battle _fresh_ from the embraces of Andromache; and it was his wife who placed his helmet on his head.

s: Andromache is wife of Hector
q: Hector used to go to battle _fresh_ from the embraces of Andromache; and it was his wife who placed his helmet on his head.

s: Mars is wayward wayward
q: Mars is wayward, and Venus is uncertain;

s: Venus is uncertain uncertain
q: Mars is wayward, and Venus is uncertain;

s: Cupid has camp Cupid's camp
q: Every lover is a soldier, and Cupid has a camp of his own;

s: Mars is caught by chains (chains wrought at the forge)
q: Mars, too, when caught, was sensible of the chains wrought at the forge;

s: Naso is slothful slothful (by former habit and disposition)
q: I myself was of slothful habit, and born for a lazy inactivity;

s: Naso is enervated by couch (along with the shade)
q: the couch and the shade [149] had enervated my mind.

s: Naso is enervated by shade (along with the couch)
q: the couch and the shade [149] had enervated my mind.

s: attentions to the charming fair gives fillip to Naso (in his indolence)
q: Attentions to the charming fair gave a fillip to me, in my indolence;

s: Naso serves in Cupid's camp (under Love's command)
q: and _Love_ commanded me to serve [150] in his camp.

s: Naso is active active (as a result of serving Love)
q: Hence it is that thou seest me active, and waging the warfare by night.

s: Naso wages warfare (by night)
q: Hence it is that thou seest me active, and waging the warfare by night.

s: Love is a warfare (as a species of warfare)
q: Cupid has a camp of his own; believe me, Atticus, [138] every lover is a soldier.

s: anxious lover is a soldier (in the sphere of Love)
q: Every lover is a soldier, and Cupid has a camp of his own; believe me, Atticus, [138] every lover is a soldier.

s: anxious lover shares condition with soldier (both pass sleepless nights and rest upon the ground)
q: Both _soldier and lover_ pass sleepless nights; both rest upon the ground.
